claim: Approximately 537 million adults are living with diabetes.
source: Diabetes is the third most common threat to human health, approximately 537 million adults living with diabetes, of which type 2 diabetes patients account for more than 90% of all diabetic patients.
evidence: This is a factual statement about diabetes prevalence presented in the introduction without specific citation, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Type 2 diabetes patients account for more than 90% of all diabetic patients.
source: Diabetes is the third most common threat to human health, approximately 537 million adults living with diabetes, of which type 2 diabetes patients account for more than 90% of all diabetic patients.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the proportion of type 2 diabetes among all diabetes cases, representing established epidemiological knowledge.

claim: Cardiac complications are the most common causes of death and disability associated with diabetes.
source: Cardiac complications are the most common causes of death and disability associated with diabetes.
evidence: This statement is presented as established medical knowledge about diabetes complications.

claim: Hyperglycemia is the key initiating factor of diabetic cardiomyopathy.
source: As the key initiating factor of diabetic cardiomyopathy, hyperglycemia can prevent optimal utilization of glucose by cardiomyocytes, which leads to myocardial fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about the pathophysiology of diabetic cardiomyopathy.

claim: Hyperglycemia can prevent optimal utilization of glucose by cardiomyocytes, which leads to myocardial fibrosis.
source: As the key initiating factor of diabetic cardiomyopathy, hyperglycemia can prevent optimal utilization of glucose by cardiomyocytes, which leads to myocardial fibrosis.
evidence: This describes a mechanistic pathway from hyperglycemia to myocardial fibrosis, representing established pathophysiological knowledge.

claim: Myocardial fibrosis is characterized by the increase in extracellular matrix proteins, deposition of interstitial collagen, disarrangement of cardiomyocytes, and the remodeling of cardiac structure.
source: Myocardial fibrosis is characterized by the increase in extracellular matrix proteins, deposition of interstitial collagen, disarrangement of cardiomyocytes, and the remodeling of cardiac structure (Russo and Frangogiannis, 2016; Jia et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Russo and Frangogiannis, 2016; Jia et al., 2018).

claim: Adult mammalian cardiomyocytes are incapable of regeneration.
source: Since adult mammalian cardiomyocytes are incapable of regeneration, the most extensive pathological extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrosis occur during various heart diseases caused by cardiomyocyte death (Kong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an established biological fact and supported by citation to Kong et al., 2014.

claim: The most extensive pathological extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrosis occur during various heart diseases caused by cardiomyocyte death.
source: Since adult mammalian cardiomyocytes are incapable of regeneration, the most extensive pathological extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrosis occur during various heart diseases caused by cardiomyocyte death (Kong et al., 2014).

claim: Mammalian hearts consist of many cell types, including cardiomyocytes, macrophages, fibroblasts and endothelial cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Banerjee et al., 2007; Litviňuková et al., 2020).

claim: Cell-to-cell communication is a fundamental feature of adult complex organs.
source: Cell-to-cell communication is a fundamental feature of adult complex organs.
evidence: This is stated as an established biological principle.

claim: Different types of cells communicate through interactions with ligand–receptor, where a ligand may be secreted and bind to a receptor, or through the fusion of two adjacent interacting cell membranes.
source: These different types of cells communicate through interactions with ligand–receptor, where a ligand may be secreted and bind to a receptor, or through the fusion of two adjacent interacting cell membranes (Ramilowski et al., 2015).

claim: The maintenance of heart homeostasis depends on intercellular communication.
source: The maintenance of heart homeostasis depends on intercellular communication (Ramilowski et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ramilowski et al., 2015.

claim: The study classified 32,585 cardiac cells from 6 healthy controls (16,490 cells) and 6 HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice (16,095 cells) into 25 transcriptionally distinct pre-clusters.
source: We classified 32,585 cardiac cells from 6 healthy controls (16,490 cells) and 6 HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice (16,095 cells) into 25 transcriptionally distinct pre-clusters that exhibited highly consistent expression patterns across individual mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Supplementary file 1), and identified 14 populations (Figure 1A) based on cell-specific markers and significantly enriched genes.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental data obtained from the scRNA-seq analysis performed in this study.

claim: The 25 pre-clusters exhibited highly consistent expression patterns across individual mice.

claim: 14 cell populations were identified based on cell-specific markers and significantly enriched genes.

claim: Endothelial cells are characterized by expression of Pecam1, Ccdc85a, and Btnl9.

claim: Macrophages are characterized by expression of Fcgr1, F13a1, and Adgre1.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and Supplementary file 2, with statistical testing (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05, log2FC ≥0.36).

claim: Among the top upregulated genes in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes were transcripts for Pdk4, Angptl4, Txnip, Postn, Hmgcs2, and Ucp3.
source: Among the top upregulated genes in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes within each cell population were transcripts for Pdk4, Angptl4, Txnip, Postn, Hmgcs2, and Ucp3, of which several have been previously involved in heart failure (Yoshioka et al., 2007; Lang et al., 2018; Sheeran et al., 2019; Koenig et al., 2022).

claim: Several of the top upregulated genes (Pdk4, Angptl4, Txnip, Postn, Hmgcs2, and Ucp3) have been previously involved in heart failure.

claim: The top 30 KEGG pathways within fibroblast population were associated with dilated cardiomyopathy, cardiac muscle contraction, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
source: The top 30 KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) pathways within fibroblast population were associated with dilated cardiomyopathy, cardiac muscle contraction, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05).

claim: 2118 unique differentially expressed genes (uni-DEGs) were identified associated with each of the major cardiac cell types.
source: To determine whether distinct cardiac cell populations respond heterogeneously to diabetic stimuli, we compared differentially expressed genes in all cardiac cell types and identified 2118 unique differentially expressed genes (uni-DEGs) associated with each of the major cardiac cell types (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is based on differential gene expression analysis performed in the study.

claim: Most of the uni-DEGs (96.6%) were detected in cardiomyocytes (32.8%), fibroblasts (18.5%), macrophages (17.7%), endothelial cells (19.7%), and endocardial cells (7.9%).
source: Most of the uni-DEGs (96.6%) were detected in cardiomyocytes (32.8%), fibroblasts (18.5%), macrophages (17.7%), endothelial cells (19.7%), and endocardial cells (7.9%).
evidence: This claim is based on quantitative analysis of the uni-DEGs distribution across cell types.

claim: The genes that were most highly expressed in only a single-cell type were Gm20658 (fibroblasts), Ucp3 (cardiomyocytes), Spock2 (endocardial cells), Irf7 (endothelial cells), and Ifi206 (macrophages).
source: The genes that were most highly expressed in only a single-cell type were Gm20658 (fibroblasts), Ucp3 (cardiomyocytes), Spock2 (endocardial cells), Irf7 (endothelial cells), and Ifi206 (macrophages), of which Ucp3 and Irf7 were involved in heart failure and pathological cardiac hypertrophy (Jiang et al., 2014; Senatus et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is based on gene expression analysis from the study.

claim: Ucp3 and Irf7 were involved in heart failure and pathological cardiac hypertrophy.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature (Jiang et al., 2014; Senatus et al., 2020).

claim: GO analysis of the uni-DEGs (upregulated) showed that terms associated with collagen fibril organization and extracellular matrix remodeling were enriched in the cardiac fibroblasts.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of the uni-DEGs (upregulated) showed that terms associated with collagen fibril organization and extracellular matrix remodeling were enriched in the cardiac fibroblasts (Figure 2A , two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05), indicating that fibroblasts are key cellular contributors to extracellular matrix remodeling and cardiac fibrosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis data shown in Figure 2A, with statistical testing (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05).

claim: Fibroblasts are key cellular contributors to extracellular matrix remodeling and cardiac fibrosis.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of the uni-DEGs (upregulated) showed that terms associated with collagen fibril organization and extracellular matrix remodeling were enriched in the cardiac fibroblasts (Figure 2A , two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05), indicating that fibroblasts are key cellular contributors to extracellular matrix remodeling and cardiac fibrosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the GO analysis results showing enrichment of ECM-related terms in fibroblasts.

claim: The endothelial and fibroblast clusters are prominent hubs for autocrine and paracrine signaling.
source: The results showed that the endothelial and fibroblast clusters are prominent hubs for autocrine and paracrine signaling (Figure 2C, D, Supplementary file 9, Supplementary file 10, FDR ≤0.01, log2FC ≥1), and that intercellular signaling in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes had changed in all cardiac cells, with fibroblasts showing the greatest increase in the number of connections (Figure 2E–G, Supplementary file 11, Supplementary file 12 and two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05, log2FC ≥0.36).
evidence: This claim is supported by ligand-receptor interaction analysis shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Intercellular signaling in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes had changed in all cardiac cells, with fibroblasts showing the greatest increase in the number of connections.

claim: Both Pdgfb and Pdgfd transcripts were upregulated in endothelial cells in diabetic mice.

claim: Pdgfc levels were significantly elevated in the macrophages of diabetic mice.
source: Both Pdgfb and Pdgfd transcripts were upregulated in endothelial cells, while Pdgfc levels were significantly elevated in the macrophages of diabetic mice (Figure 3C, D and two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05, log2FC ≥0.36).

claim: The Egfr ligand Efemp1 was upregulated in the epicardial cells.

claim: HFD/STZ treatment significantly increased cardiac p-Pdgfra protein levels.

claim: Ima treatment decreased p-Pdgfra levels in the HFD/STZ + Ima group compared with the HFD/STZ group.
source: The results showed that HFD/STZ treatment significantly increased cardiac p-Pdgfra protein levels and decreased that of p-Pdgfra in the HFD/STZ + Ima group compared with the HFD/STZ group (Figure 3F, n = 6 mice per group).

claim: The myocardium of the HFD/STZ-treated mice expressed higher levels of Col1a1 and Col3a1 compared with the control group.

claim: Ima treatment attenuated the increase in HFD/STZ-induced collagen synthesis and deposition.

claim: Pdgf(s)–Pdgfra interactions contribute to diabetic myocardial fibrosis.

claim: Unsupervised Seurat-based clustering of the 6416 fibroblasts revealed 10 distinct subpopulations.

claim: Fibroblast subpopulation 3 formed a distinct cluster from other fibroblast subpopulations, based on its expression pattern.
source: The analysis revealed that fibroblast subpopulation 3 formed a distinct cluster from other fibroblast subpopulations, based on its expression pattern (Figure 4B).

claim: The top enriched genes in subpopulation 3 (Nppa and Clu) and subpopulation 5 (Postn and Cilp) are well-established biomarkers of pro-fibrotic function.

claim: Fibroblast 3 and 5 populations were strongly involved in extracellular matrix remodeling and collagen synthesis.

claim: Fibroblast 3 and 5 subpopulations are myocardial fibrosis-related cardiac fibroblast subpopulations.

claim: The most significantly enriched gene in subpopulation 3 was Hrc.

claim: Hrc is crucial for proper cardiac function through the regulation of Ca2+-uptake, storage, and release.

claim: The most significantly enriched gene in fibroblast subpopulation 5 was Postn.

claim: Postn-enriched fibroblast subset is consistent with the fibroblast subset identified in an animal model of angiotensin-induced myocardial hypertrophy.

claim: Mef2a was enriched in subpopulations 7 and 8.

claim: HFD/STZ treatment induced transcriptional changes in all cardiac fibroblast subpopulations.

claim: The upregulated genes in the Hrchi fibroblasts were enriched in GO terms such as collagen fiber reorganization and extracellular matrix binding.
source: HFD/STZ treatment induced transcriptional changes in all cardiac fibroblast subpopulations (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Supplementary files 19, and two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05, log2FC ≥0.36), and the upregulated genes in the Hrchi fibroblasts were enriched in GO terms such as collagen fiber reorganization and extracellular matrix binding (Figure 6A and two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 6A with statistical testing (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR ≤0.05).

claim: The top 20 enriched pathways in the Hrchi fibroblasts of the diabetic group were associated with extracellular matrix organization, myocardial fibrosis, and fibroblast activation.

claim: The Hrchi fibroblasts are key cellular drivers of myocardial fibrosis in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes.
source: These results suggest that the Hrchi fibroblasts are key cellular drivers of myocardial fibrosis in response to HFD/STZ-induced diabetes.

claim: Lgals3bp and Fn1 were upregulated in the heart tissues of diabetic mice.

claim: The level of Itgb1 mRNA decreased by >80% in response to a single injection of Itgb1 siRNA, compared with the negative control.

claim: The knockdown of Itgb1 lasted for more than 5 months after the injection of the siRNA.

claim: Levels of collagen synthesis and deposition were downregulated in the Itgb1 knockout mice.

claim: Itgb1 in Hrchi fibroblasts contributes to HFD/STZ-induced myocardial fibrosis.

claim: Pdgfra phosphorylation was significantly promoted in the DB/DB mice.

claim: The phosphorylation level of Pdgfra was significantly inhibited after Ima treatment in DB/DB mice.

claim: Hrc was highly expressed in DB/DB diabetic mice and overlaps with the fibroblast marker Desmin.

claim: Hrc is significantly activated in the fibroblasts of the diabetic heart.

claim: Ima treatment significantly inhibited the expression of Hrc and Desmin in DB/DB mice.

claim: Ima treatment could significantly inhibit the accumulation of collagen fibers in the heart of the diabetic mice.
